newsitem.title: INDIA: India metals steady, port stocks pile-up on strike.
newsitem.headline: India metals steady, port stocks pile-up on strike.

text.p: Indian base metals on Monday remained steady in a narrow price range on the local market, dealers said.
Demand from industrial consumers remained low but the absence of fresh arrivals kept prices at previous levels.

"Inflow of imported metal from the Bombay port to the market remained virtually absent since a week on account of a nationwide strike called by the transport operators," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
"Different ships carrying imported metals are halted at Bombay port and about 1,000 tonnes of imported metals are piled up at port while we are facing shortage of ready stock in the market," he said.

Metals' offtake from the market by industrial consumers also remained very slow due to the truckers strike. Copper was traded at 13,500 rupees while zinc was quiet at 7,850 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal. Aluminium remained steady at 7,450 rupees, tin at 31,600 rupees and nickel at 36,800 rupees per quintal on nominal activity.
Indian transporters are on strike since April 1, protesting a service charge as well as hike in the insurance premium.
The Bombay metals market is closed on Tuesday for a local Hindu festival and will reopen on Wednesday for trading.
